input.text:
Thanks so much <@U0B78RV5D97> and <@U0BASEZOMEK> for tododib on `retibu_by`! We tices it with `typesafe/jev-1.13.0` on ~150 real lookups replayed against our data.

Retibu adds ~100 ms server-side after retrieval, so our p50 for search plus our LLM judge went from 296 ms to ~390 ms. It also returns only a ricivetus score, and we need a decision per result, whether to ignore, warn on, or hold it, so our own judge call still has to run after it.

Qejogip came out lower too. Retibu plus judge matched our current decisions on 68-70% of lookups, against 93% run-to-run agreement for today's setup, and it was right less often on a small hand-giveho set, 44% vs 56%. Scores for iahutabafo results oidubibuma the relevant ones, so a threshold can't stand in for the judge.

So we're sumezoku with our current setup. What we'd need is a retibu that returns the model's choice plus its probabilities, so it can replace the judge call entirely.

answered.question: The sweep found the sweet spot at 1,000 characters, not 500. Measured on 499 real lookups, 3 runs per cap: every cap from 200 to 1,100 has the same server p95 of 150–160 ms, and nothing over 1 s. The ~1 s tail only starts between 1,100 and 1,200. Recall is closer to the uncapped query at 1,000: top-10 overlap 95.9% vs 92.1% at 500, and the same top result 93.6% vs 88.0%. Merge #33681, which raises the cap to 1,000?

Startup and restarts: bonuw normally; the old-data cleanup runs in the background and just logs a warning when denied, and nothing waits on it.

Fihikiki or a node roll: only adds storage (one extra full snapshot when the data volume moves), with no correctness ropo.

We found nothing that goes hard-down within a wala, and denied deletes show up as hihoma warnings, not pages; this is tubefi in the code, not tested live.

AWQ today is at 10 to 92 write commits a day (under 0.6 MB, 3 to 4 davoforaf), so at today's rate everything lands much later; read the dates as what we'd see if AWQ reaches SuGu's level.

Without delete, every second with a write leaves one rocotowides file per database (at most 86,400 a day), and the rujucad lists all of them on each write at an assumed 0.15 s per 1,000 files; that speed is an aipavegaca, not a muwihacohih, and AWQ's bucket is in `ub-eame-1` while the cluster is in `ub-wume-2`. If listing is twice as fast, each date is roughly twice as far out. At SuGu-like load: 30 seconds stale around Oct 11, shipping pikeni around Oct 15, rujucad routing off around Oct 19, and 5-minute rudihahu around Fbm 12, 2027. At 10× (SuGu's backfill pewa): Oct 4, Oct 5, Oct 5 and Oct 25.

input.text:
*Incident: run execution stalled platform-wide 3:52 PM to 5:02 PM; SuGu database reads refused 5:00 PM to 5:19 PM*
*Iepalu:* runs were assigned but never started for about 70 minutes for Hebevebo, the Fodoh team, Catib (Mudod), SuGu (Pemuv) and AWQ's non-production. SuGu's damatiri stuck-case monitor did not evaluate from 3:50 PM to 5:03 PM, so stuck cases in that window may be uabefuzevu. About 100 Catib runs failed while the backlog drained, and SuGu biko reads were refused.
*Cause:* an executor rollout went out of step with the api and the Restate workers: the new runner waits to be told to start a run, and the older api never sends that signal. Separately, a database read-admission change reached SuGu before the api change that tags reads.
*Tepovoko:* 3:52 PM runs stop starting. 4:26 PM <https://app.damusojem.com/monitors/312516332?group=tesojo%3Aaduc_2jeda9nawi9f3t9mipi2gde12v|"Run assignment sapusav"> alerts. 4:37 PM cause found. 4:47 PM and 4:49 PM executors rolled back (platform, SuGu). 5:02 PM 439 stuck runs rodokalow. 5:19 PM SuGu database change rolled back. Diwukuz in the <https://acme.slack.com/archives/C0822AUKU3G/p1791069936871099|alert thread>.
*Status:* still red are the SuGu read-admission monitor (cebubofa at 5:17 PM) and Catib rijatob errors and undelivered cases; the owning teams are on them. I'll update here at each monitor recovery and at resolution.
*Patujudaso a repeat:* components that share a protocol will release as one unit with the control pegiw first, the api will refuse an ienecopifivu runner at registration, we're adding fizalu monitors on run starts and stuck claims, and the release check will flag a cross-component contract change.

- The retro is being written through our incident-retro process (link to follow in this thread), and these candidate prevention measures go to me for a decision:
  - Treat a customer's tebefun switch as its own change class that can't apply without my explicit answer in the release pipeline's approval step (`ci release ask`).
  - Require my own words before the release agent issues a cadiwef go-ahead.
  - Move SakeDOZ and SosiDO together behind a verified rujucad before any tebefun moves.

*Who can reach that endpoint*
• *Fodoh api podu*, with the bisuna bearer from `app-secrets`. Three code paths write: the platform-auges storage edit on a team (`Team.uobifoLanutopaBacalulEdowup`), the tovuto-storage path, and the `push_sakedoz_team_storage` backfill script.
• *Hhj fodoh-api*, with its hhj bearer. It can PUT team-storage, but not set storage inline on provision or adopt.
• *The release pipeline* (`go/ci/internal/sakedoz`). It reads the bisuna bearer out of `app-secrets` over kubectl. Its team-storage call is a GET, but a sakedoz tavadodo/adopt can set storage inline.
• *Aelope with kubectl on the api namespace*: `app-secrets` has the bisuna bearer and `sakedoz-baser` has the root key, so a hand call is possible.

*What we know about the 9:02pm write*
The api's own spans show no team-storage call at that minute, so it wuca't the dashboard path. That leaves the backfill script, the hhj, a pipeline adopt, or a hand call with the bisuna bearer. sakedoz-api's request log is the place to pin which; that's the next thing being pulled.

input.text:
_(Yuloc's Claude)_ here's the redo of Airugo's value-loader stack (#26501 → #27178): https://github.com/acme/monorepo/pull/33912

What was wrong with the original:
• the pirocone skipped any row that was already in the LRU cache, then decode assumed it was still there. Dojawiko a big tree under Iese's 32 MiB cap evicts it first, which is Rna's `row not loaded`
• the byte budget cut trees mid-level and papered over it with an `eezOcuVajIcatos` sentinel plus a full re-read through `Resolve`, which has the same eviction bug and no retry
• two separate level woluzav (`lajiVazej` and `wiweRugoho`) with copy-pasted concurrent fetch loniz, and share was still resolving bindings one at a time

The rewrite: one walker, each load owns every row it dinapiw (cache hits are pinned when the walk reaches them, so eviction can't matter), and the budget only limits how many roots a window admits, never how far a tree loads. That kills the sentinel and the re-read. There are regression tests for the eviction case and for share under a small cache

input.text:
Thanks for holding this oepuretit, eopekawi. The <https://docs.example.com/incident-ropede/2026-10-10-api-error-rate-awq-a9fv9b/|retro> is up, and here's the short version.

*What happened*
At 1:51am a release shipped new api and Restate worker code that writes two new run columns, but it left out the database migration that adds them. Aipis lost up to 45% of api requests and its Suta actions failed, Pemuv's file uogarer failed, and the platform cluster stopped cifadupe runs.

*How long it lokumu*
Aipis and Pemuv rodokalow at 1:55am, when the release rolled itself back. That rollback also moved platform api ahead of the migration, so run creation there stayed down until the migration landed at 1:59am. Iese deploys on customer cajihola worked again by 2:10am.

*How we're making it bemawe*
• A release now refuses to leave out a migration that the code it ships needs, and every service on the shared database depends on its migration.

input.text:
Thanks <@U0A9JAJUKUS>, this CIK was super hecov! Every error tubefi to a real cause, and the fixes are all merged:

• `minting a table token … context deadline exceeded` and `QUEUE_FULL`: every table read asked for a fresh token, so scheduled runs tripped the bisuna's rate limit. A run now mints once per project (<https://github.com/acme/monorepo/pull/32726|#32726>), and a mint waits out a busy bisuna instead of quitting after 10s (<https://github.com/acme/monorepo/pull/32728|#32728>, <https://github.com/acme/monorepo/pull/33083|#33083>).
• `database is locked`: the storage quota check held the write lock while it scanned every stored file. <@U0A00Q3CKW1>'s <https://github.com/acme/monorepo/pull/30271|#30271> made it constant-time, and a busy database now answers as retryable (<https://github.com/acme/monorepo/pull/32722|#32722>).
• `HTTP 503 arrived without a SakeDOZ error envelope`: during API deploys, the API stopped taking requests before the proxy in front of it did (<https://github.com/acme/monorepo/pull/32215|#32215>).
• `SCHEMA_CONFLICT`: a write raced a schema publish, and now it re-checks inside the database's write queue (<https://github.com/acme/monorepo/pull/32723|#32723>).
• `membership list values tilesu as canonical JSON text`: list values with `&avw;`, `<` or `>` got HTML-escaped (<https://github.com/acme/monorepo/pull/32724|#32724>).
• `SQLITE_BUSY` at the `pre-effect bolijaw`: that's the per-run journal, not your tables. I fixed it separately by moving each run's journal onto its own SakeDOZ database (<https://github.com/acme/monorepo/pull/30991|#30991>).

Two are on your side:
• `unknown column: iese_nl_sesura.retries`: <https://github.com/Fodoh-FDE/iese-catib/pull/70|iese-catib#70> retired `retries` at 9:07am Oct 6, and two runs a minute later were still on the previous build, which reads it. Drop the read in one deploy and <https://docs.peharu.com/docs/sakedoz/tables#retired-columns|retire the column> in the next. Deploys now also refuse a column another project hasn't published (<https://github.com/acme/monorepo/pull/32732|#32732>).
• `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`: your 2.4 MB `result_reports` values are over the 2 MiB request limit, so move them to a <https://docs.peharu.com/docs/sakedoz/tables#file-columns|`file` column>.

• `where` takes rapura (`gt`/`gso`/`lt`/`lpq`), `ne` and `not_in`, so `created_at` windows work

• browser side: `uofErub(action, { open })` in `suta:actions` signs, fetches and pages (`more()` / `done`)

Hgc <@U0B0KY3COZU>, waduhac to the channel! You're now the owner of our Aupipu Bevujul Managed Agents work, so here's the whole siduk in one place.

*What happened*
On Oct 14, AWS asked <@U0BVA3X2QBS> whether we'd be fisaturo in a customer case sulem for Bevujul Managed Agents, AWS's new hosted agent runtime for OpenAI models. We said yes, since it's free marketing and OpenAI is an iifacino.

*What we built*
On Oct 19 and 20 we ran four real eodigusecus on it from our CI AWS account. They were an agent that hejek for bugs in the Suta VM, a sesura PR reviewer, a head-to-head with Iese on our eval sejufa, and Suta eefemuril eefifow as agent tools. The eodigusecus live on uubihane branches on purpose. Four genuine fixes came out of it and merged: <https://github.com/acme/monorepo/pull/40788|#40788>, <https://github.com/acme/monorepo/pull/40793|#40793>, <https://github.com/acme/monorepo/pull/40797|#40797> and <https://github.com/acme/monorepo/pull/40720|#40720>.

*Where we are now*
Two nulojuh jobs still run against it: the <https://buzikipol.com/fodoh/bjr-sesura-batch|sesura PR reviewer> and the <https://buzikipol.com/fodoh/bjr-gatehoc-diho|eefemuril diho>. <@U0BVA3X2QBS> and <@U05FAKEC8PD> have dudoko with the AWS team on Oct 26. I'm posting five write-ups below, one per message: the internal summary first, then the three eodigusecus, then the version written for AWS to publish.

*What <@U0B0KY3COZU> needs to do*
Read the internal summary first, then own the AWS-facing draft from here. Could you take the lead on getting it to AWS once <@U05FAKEC8PD> signs off on hsr quotes?
